questions.question: Picture a triangle card with its three corners labelled. The angles are 90°, 55° and 35°. Maya turns the card so the 90° corner points straight down. What kind of triangle is it by its angles?
options: A right triangle, because one angle is exactly 90°
An acute triangle, because 55° and 35° are both acute
A scalene triangle only — it stops being a right triangle once the 90° corner points down
An obtuse triangle, because 90° is the largest angle
questions.explain: A triangle is named by its largest angle, and exactly one 90° angle makes it a right triangle. Turning the card moves the corners but does not change any angle, so it is still right; and 90° is not 'more than 90°', so it is not obtuse.

questions.question: Picture a triangle card with three corners. The angles are 100°, 45° and 35°. What kind of triangle is it by its angles?
options: Acute, because two of the three angles are less than 90°
Obtuse, because one angle is greater than 90°
Right, because 100° is close to a square corner
You cannot name it until you know which corner is at the bottom
questions.explain: Look at the largest angle only: 100° is more than 90°, so the triangle is obtuse. A triangle can have two acute angles and still be obtuse, and the way it sits on the page never changes its type.

questions.question: Picture a triangle card whose three angles are all 60°. What kind of triangle is it by its angles?
options: Obtuse, because 60° + 60° = 120°, which is more than 90°
It is equilateral, so it cannot also be given an angle name
Acute, because all three angles are less than 90°
Acute when the card points up, but obtuse when the card points down
questions.explain: Compare each angle to 90° one at a time: 60°, 60° and 60° are all smaller, so every angle is acute and the triangle is acute. Do not add two angles together, and remember a triangle gets both a side name (equilateral) and an angle name (acute).

questions.question: Picture a triangle card with angles 90°, 45° and 45°, resting so that the square corner is up at the top right. What kind of triangle is it by its angles?
options: Acute, because there are two acute angles and only one that is not
Obtuse, because the two equal angles make it lean over
Not a right triangle — the square corner has to sit at the bottom for that
Right, because one angle is exactly 90°
questions.explain: One 90° angle is enough to make a triangle right, no matter how many acute angles are beside it. A right triangle stays right whether the square corner is at the bottom, the top or the side.

questions.question: Two angles of a triangle measure 35° and 40°. What kind of triangle is it by its angles?
options: Obtuse, because the third angle is 105°, which is greater than 90°
Right, because the leftover angle is bigger than 90° and any angle over 90° is a right angle
You cannot tell until you know which way the triangle is pointing
Acute, because 35° and 40° are both acute angles
questions.explain: First find the missing angle: 180° − 35° − 40° = 105°. Then compare the largest angle to 90°: 105° is bigger, so the triangle is obtuse. The trap is judging only the two angles you were given.

questions.question: Ben is cutting a triangular sail for a model boat. Two of its angles measure 55° and 35°. What kind of triangle is the sail by its angles?
options: Acute, because both of the given angles are less than 90°
Right, because the missing angle is 90°
Obtuse, because 180° − 55° = 125°, which is more than 90°
It depends — flipped so the biggest angle is on top, the sail becomes acute
questions.explain: Subtract both known angles from 180°: 180° − 55° − 35° = 90°, so the sail is a right triangle. A common slip is subtracting only one angle, which leaves 125° and makes the sail look obtuse.

questions.question: Which set of three angle measures belongs to an acute triangle?
options: 25°, 65°, 90° — it is acute once you turn it so the 90° corner is on top
questions.explain: A triangle is acute only when every angle is under 90°, and 70°, 60° and 50° all are. One 90° angle makes a right triangle and one angle over 90° makes an obtuse triangle, no matter how the triangle is turned.

questions.question: Priya builds a triangle on her geoboard with angles 90°, 60° and 30°. She then rotates the whole board a quarter turn. Which statement is true after the turn?
options: It is now obtuse, because the longest side ends up on top
It has no angle type any more; only its sides can be named now
It becomes acute, because rotating makes the largest angle smaller
It is still a right triangle, because the angles are still 90°, 60° and 30°
questions.explain: Rotating a shape slides the corners to new spots but every angle keeps its exact measure, so a 90° angle stays 90° and the triangle stays right. Type comes from the angle measures, never from which side is on top.

questions.question: At Kitsilano Beach, Noah holds a triangular kite panel with angles of 25° and 65° at its two lower corners. His sister takes it and holds it upside down, then says the panel changed its type. How should the panel be classified by its angles?
options: Right in both positions, because the third angle is 180° − 25° − 65° = 90°
Obtuse while it is upside down, and right while it is upright
Acute in both positions, because 25° and 65° are both acute angles
Right while upright, but with no angle type at all once it is upside down
questions.explain: Find the missing angle first: 180° − 25° − 65° = 90°, so the panel is a right triangle. Flipping or turning it moves the 90° corner to a new place but does not resize it, so the type cannot change.

questions.question: A roof truss for a garden shed is a triangle. Its two bottom angles are both 30°, and the third angle is at the peak. How is the truss classified by its angles?
options: Acute, because the two bottom angles are only 30°, and small angles make an acute triangle
Obtuse, because the peak angle is 180° − 30° − 30° = 120°, which is more than 90°
Right, because a roof always meets the walls in square corners
It is isosceles, so it is acute — and its type would change if the truss were turned over
questions.explain: Work out the peak angle, 180° − 30° − 30° = 120°, then compare it to 90°: it is larger, so the truss is obtuse. Two small base angles do not make a triangle acute, because only the largest angle decides the type.

questions.question: Ava sorts triangle cards into three bins labelled acute, right and obtuse. Her cards show 80°, 60°, 40° / 60°, 60°, 60° / 90°, 45°, 45° tipped onto a slanted side / 95°, 50°, 35°. Which card belongs in the obtuse bin?
options: The card with 80°, 60°, 40°
The card with 60°, 60°, 60°
The card with 95°, 50°, 35°
The card with 90°, 45°, 45°, because it is tipped onto its slanted side
questions.explain: Check the largest angle on each card: only 95° is greater than 90°, so that card is the obtuse one. A card with a 90° angle goes in the right bin even when it is tipped over, because tipping does not change the measure.

questions.question: Liam says a right triangle stops being a right triangle as soon as you turn it so the square corner points down. What is the best reason he is wrong?
options: He is not wrong — a right triangle must have its square corner at the bottom left
He is wrong because a triangle with a 90° angle is really named by its sides, not its angles
He is wrong because a turned right triangle becomes an obtuse triangle instead
Turning a triangle moves it but does not change any angle measure, so the 90° angle is still there
questions.explain: A triangle is classified by the size of its angles, and turning or flipping it keeps every measure exactly the same, so the 90° angle survives the turn. Angle names (acute, right, obtuse) and side names (scalene, isosceles, equilateral) are two separate labels, and neither depends on which way the shape faces.
